name: 44787-multiimage-qwen3vl8b-1gpu
model: Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct -- public, ungated, image-text-to-text, ~17 GB of bf16 safetensors.
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine (guidellm's `vllm_python` backend).
architecture: Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration, bf16: a 36-layer language model (hidden 4096, 32 query / 8 KV heads, head_dim 128) behind a 27-layer vision tower; the rest is in the checkpoint's own config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=4, warmup 10%, cooldown 10%, bounded at 400 requests with a 1800 s safety cap.
workload: four-page multi-image chat: four DISTINCT 1792x2528 JPEG pages (`content: noise`, quality 40, seeds 42-45) plus a 1024-token instruction per request, answered in 16 tokens. Five guidellm datasets zipped row-wise -- one `synthetic_text` and FOUR `synthetic_image` generators each with `images_per_request: 1`, which is required: a count above one emits `image_0 .. image_3`, guidellm reads a trailing `_N` as a conversation TURN, and the in-process backend refuses every turn past the first. Each page is 4.53 Mpx and both sides are exact multiples of the processor's patch x merge = 32 px quantum, so it is neither rescaled nor rounded: 4,424 prompt tokens per page, ~18.8k per request.
purpose: A document question-answering assistant reading four scanned pages per request, four concurrent users, short answers, single GPU.
launch:
# The engine's command line: vLLM at commit 4559c43a9526597c00cbcc4f59979496500268d1
# (v0.23.1rc0-552-g4559c43a9526). Interpreter and hardware seal are in configs/env.yaml.

model: Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct
tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16

# ~18.8k prompt tokens + 16 generated per request; the next ceiling above the workload. The
# checkpoint advertises 262144, which here would only enlarge the startup profiling pass.
max-model-len: 20480

# Above scenario.json's 4 streams, so the operating point is the stream count, not this ceiling.
max-num-seqs: 8

# Must match scenario.json, which puts FOUR pictures in every request. KEEP THIS VALUE ON ONE
# LINE as inline JSON: the config reader takes a value only from its key's own line and skips
# indented ones, so a block mapping is dropped whole and the per-modality default of 1 applies.
limit-mm-per-prompt: {"image": 4}

# The engine default at this commit, written out so a later default cannot drift it.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
